BURHAN:v3p293/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p293/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p293/r2.claim: In the partial-reversal pattern, the second word is formed from letters of the first while some letters remain in both; بني is composed from بين.
BURHAN:v3p293/r2.anchor: وهو أن تكون الكلمة الثانية مركبة من حروف الكلمة الأولى مع بقاء بعض حروف الكلمة الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p370#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p370#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p370#2/r1.claim: لحية is the familiar word for beard; its plural لحى is pronounced with either kasra or damma on the lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p370#2/r1.anchor: اللحية معروفة وتجمع على لحى بكسر اللام وضمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r8.speaker: عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r8.claim: Isa ibn Sulayman al-Hijazi reads بلحيتي with fatḥa on the lām, a Hijazi dialect form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r8.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي بلحيتي بفتح اللام وهي لغة أهل الحجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r9.claim: Moses, fiercely jealous for God's religion, seized Aaron by his hair and beard; Aaron explains that fighting would have caused mutual division and destruction, so he waited for Moses to restore order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r9.anchor: وكان موسى عليه السلام شديد الغضب لله ولدينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r10.claim: Abu Jafar reads ولم ترقب with a ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on qāf, as the imperfect of أرقب.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p374/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ولم ترقب بضم التاء وكسر القاف مضارع أرقب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r1.claim: Moses’ grasping Aaron’s beard and head reflects both religious honor and natural brotherly love; prophets tolerate worldly matters but do not compromise in religion, especially with those close to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r1.anchor: in religious affairs, they do not compromise in any way.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r2.claim: Worldly-minded people show the reverse pattern: cautious in worldly affairs, they lack sensitivity when close relatives err in religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r2.anchor: in religious affairs, they do not have any sensitivity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r3.claim: Aaron says he tried to stop the people, but Sāmirī’s spell swayed most of them and Aaron feared for his life; separating with his followers risked division and bloodshed, so he waited for Moses’ return and authority.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p62/r3.anchor: The first option would have resulted in divisions among people and bloodshed.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.claim: They read ابن أم with fatḥa on mīm; Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission use kasra, with hamza still ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p294/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم ﴿ قال ابن أم ﴾ نصبا وفى طه 94 مثله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p422/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p422/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p422/r7.claim: They read يا ابن أم with fatḥa on mīm; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Ibn Amir use kasra.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p422/r7.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم / يبنؤم / بفتح الميم

NAHHAS:v3p54/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p54/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p54/r20.claim: With fatḥa, ibn umm joins two nouns as one; with kasra, it is a regular genitive annexation.
NAHHAS:v3p54/r20.anchor: بالفتح يجعل الاسمين اسما واحدا وبالخفض على الإضافة

NAHHAS:v3p54/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p54/r21.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v3p54/r21.claim: Abu Ishaq allows the non-Qur’anic form yā ibna ummī with a yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v3p54/r21.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق ويجوز في غير القرآن يا ابن أمي بالياء

NAHHAS:v3p54/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p54/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p54/r22.claim: Aaron asks Moses not to seize his beard or head because the people might mistake it for contempt or punishment; another report says Moses did not act from either motive.
NAHHAS:v3p54/r22.anchor: لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي ) أي لا تفعل هذا فيتوهموا أنه منك استخفاف وعقوبة وقد قيل إن موسى عليه السلام

NAHHAS:v3p54/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p54/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p54/r23.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel by leaving the people, contrary to the command to stay with them.
NAHHAS:v3p54/r23.anchor: إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ) أي خشيت أن أخرج وأتركهم وقد أمرتني أن أخرج معهم

TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r10.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r10.claim: Moses returned angry and sorrowful, threw down the tablets, and seized Aaron; Aaron said he feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel and ignoring his instruction.
TABATABAI:20:80-98#2/r10.anchor: ثم رمى بالألواح وأخذ بلحية أخيه ورأسه يجره إليه فقال { ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا أن لا تتبعني

THALABI:v6p258/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p258/r6.speaker: الكلبي وغيره
THALABI:v6p258/r6.claim: Although Aaron was Moses's full brother, he said “son of my mother” to soften Moses and make him relent; others say they shared only a mother, or that motherhood is literal while fatherhood is attributed by legal convention.
THALABI:v6p258/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي وغيره: كان أخاه لأبيه وأمه ولكنه أراد بقوله: ابن أم أن يرققه ويستعطفه عليه

THALABI:v6p258/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p258/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p258/r7.claim: Being seized by the beard or head means the forelock and head hair, honored parts singled out for respect.
THALABI:v6p258/r7.anchor: تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي يعني ذؤابتي وشعر رأسي إذ هما عضوان مصونان يقصدان بالإكرام والإعظام

THALABI:v6p258/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p258/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p258/r8.claim: Aaron feared that reproving them would split them into factions who fought each other, leading Moses to accuse him of causing division and failing to keep the instruction to succeed and reform the people.
THALABI:v6p258/r8.anchor: ني خشيت لو أنكرت عليهم لصاروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا فتقول رقت بين بني إسرائيل

THALABI:v6p258/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p258/r9.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p258/r9.claim: Qatada says the righteous had recalled the danger of division before this episode.
THALABI:v6p258/r9.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية: فذكر الصالحون الفرقة قبلكم، ثم أقبل موسى على السامرى

RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r1.claim: Rāzī reports the critics' first dilemma: if Moses ordered Aaron to follow, either Moses sinned by reproaching an innocent follower or Aaron sinned by disobeying; without an order, Moses sinned by reproaching him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن موسى عليه السلام إما أن يكون قد أمر هرون باتباعه أو لم يأمره

RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r3.claim: The critics' third argument treats Moses' seizure of Aaron as sinful whether it occurred before or after Moses learned that Aaron had done all he could to advise and restrain the people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r3.anchor: وهذا معصية لأن هارون عليه السلام قد فعل ما قدر عليه من النصيحة والوعظ والزجر

RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r4.claim: The critics' fourth dilemma is that if taking Aaron by the beard and head was permissible, Aaron sinned by forbidding it; if impermissible, Moses sinned by doing it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r4.anchor: فإن كان الأخذ بلحيته وبرأسه جائزا

RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r5.claim: Rāzī rejects charging prophets with sin from these apparent readings: his earlier proof at 2:36 establishes their immunity, and ambiguous wording cannot override evidence that admits no ready reinterpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r5.anchor: أنا بينا في سورة البقرة في تفسير قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r6.claim: For his first answer, Rāzī notes agreement that prophets may leave what is best: Moses and Aaron could differ over which of two actions was preferable without either sinning.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93/r6.anchor: أنا وإن اختلفنا في جواز المعصية على الأنبياء لكن اتفقنا على جواز ترك الأولى عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r1.claim: Rāzī answers that evidence may qualify an unqualified instruction: they could understand decisiveness as “do or omit this if you seek what is best,” leaving the condition unstated because their agreement on it was established.

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r2.claim: Moses, angry and thoughtful, may have seized and pulled Aaron as a person might bite his lip, twist his fingers, or grasp his own beard; he treated his brother and partner as himself.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r2.anchor: فأخذ برأس أخيه وجره إليه كما يفعل الإنسان بنفسه مثل ذلك عند الغضب

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r3.claim: Aaron's plea can mean he feared suspicious Israelites would misread Moses' gesture as reproach or lack of support, so he asked him not to give them that impression.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r3.anchor: فلا يمتنع أن يكون هرون عليه السلام خاف من أن يتوهم بنو إسرائيل من سوء ظنهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r4.claim: Rāzī adds that Israelites were so suspicious they accused Moses of killing Aaron during an absence; after Moses' thirty nights became forty and he returned with the Tablets, he pulled Aaron close to investigate, while Aaron feared baseless suspicion.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r4.anchor: حتى أن هارون غاب عنهم غيبة

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r5.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf attributes the act to Moses' naturally fierce, rough temper and intense anger for God: stunned at calf worship, he threw the Tablets and confronted Aaron as an enemy.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r5.anchor: كان موسى عليه السلام رجلا حديدا مجبولا على الحدة والخشونة

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r6.claim: Rāzī rejects al-Kashshāf's anger defense: if Moses remained rational and accountable, the objections remain and anger adds a sin; if not accountable, a Muslim cannot accept that.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r6.anchor: واعلم أن هذا الجواب ساقط لأنه يقال

RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r7.claim: Rāzī says these replies address those who disallow minor sins; for theologians who allow minor sins, the objection no longer stands.
RAZI-FULL:v22p93#2/r7.anchor: فهذه أجوبة من لم يجوز الصغائر وأما من جوزها فلا شك في سقوط السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r5.claim: One explanation is that Aaron called Moses “son of my mother” to soften him and make him release his hold; another is that they literally shared a mother.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r5.anchor: قيل : إنما خاطبه بذلك ليدفعه عنه فيتركه

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r6.claim: The prohibition does not prove Moses had actually seized Aaron: forbidding an act does not establish that it occurred, as in 33:48 and the conditional warning at 39:65.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r6.anchor: فإن النهي عن الشيء لا يدل على كون المنهي فاعلا

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r7.claim: Even the stated act of pulling Aaron by the head does not show contempt; it could serve any of the other purposes Rāzī has described.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r7.anchor: والذي فيه أنه أخذ برأس أخيه يجره إليه وهذا القدر لا يدل على الاستخفاف به

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r8.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r8.claim: Some say Moses took Aaron by the forelocks in his right hand and by the beard with his left.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r8.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول إنه أخذ ذؤابتيه بيمينه ولحيته بيساره

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r9.claim: Rāzī reconciles Aaron's answer with Moses' order by making the order conditional: Aaron should follow only if doing so would not cause disorder; joining Moses amid disorder would violate that condition.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r9.anchor: لعل موسى عليه السلام إنما أمره بالذهاب إليه بشرط أن لا يؤدي ذلك إلى فساد في القوم

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r10.speaker: أبو القاسم الأنصاري
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r10.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Anṣārī argues that divine guidance benefits more than signs: the magicians saw one sign, believed, and endured severe punishment without recanting.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r10.anchor: الهداية أنفع من الدلالة فإن السحرة كانوا أجانب عن الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r11.speaker: أبو القاسم الأنصاري
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r11.claim: He contrasts the Israelites, who witnessed the staff-serpent, its swallowing the magicians' displays and return to a staff, the magicians' confession, nine signs, and the divided sea and deliverance, yet still sought idols.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r11.anchor: وأما قومه فإنهم رأوا انقلاب العصا ثعبانا والتقم كل ما جمعه السحرة ثم عاد عصا

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r12.speaker: أبو القاسم الأنصاري
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r12.claim: After crossing the sea, the Israelites asked for a god like the idolaters' and worshipped the calf when they heard its sound, showing that signs alone do not achieve faith without guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r12.anchor: ثم إن هؤلاء مع ما شاهدوا من هذه الآيات لما خرجوا من البحر

RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r13.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r13.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read “yā ibn ummi” with kasra and genitive construction, the kasra signaling the omitted yāʾ; the others read with fatḥa, understood as “yā ibn ummāh.”
RAZI-FULL:v22p94/r13.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي : ( يا ابن أم ) بكسر الميم والإضافة

STUDYQURAN:20:92/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r1.claim: While Moses was on the mountain, God informed him that the people had gone astray; he returned angry and grieved.
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r1.anchor: While on the mountain, Moses was informed by God that his people had gone astray. He thus returned to them in a state of anger and grief

STUDYQURAN:20:92/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r2.claim: Seeing the Israelites worship the idol, Moses threw down the Tablets in anger and shock.
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r2.anchor: when he saw their worship of the idol, he threw down the Tablets in anger and shock

STUDYQURAN:20:92/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r3.claim: Because Moses had left Aaron in charge, he rebuked him for what happened during his absence.
STUDYQURAN:20:92/r3.anchor: Since Moses had left Aaron in charge of the Israelites, upon his return he rebuked Aaron for what had happened while he was absent

TAB-FULL:v16p146/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says Aaron feared that if he went with the believers who followed him, others would remain behind, and Moses would accuse him of splitting Israel.
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله تعالى

TAB-FULL:v16p146/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Aaron feared the Israelites would divide into two groups and kill one another until they were destroyed.
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، {إني خشيت أن تقول، فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي} [طه: 94] قال: كنا نكون فرقتين فيقتل بعضنا بعضا حتى نتفانى

TAB-FULL:v16p146/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the explanation that Moses blamed Aaron for not following his command with the believers; Aaron feared Moses would say he had split the community by leaving some behind. Aaron’s appeal to the people and their refusal to leave the calf support this reading.
TAB-FULL:v16p146/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب، القول الذي قاله ابن عباس من أن موسى عذل أخاه هارون على تركه اتباع أمره بمن اتبعه من أهل الإيمان

TAB-FULL:v16p147/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p147/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p147/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says لم ترقب قولي means ‘you did not preserve my command’; al-Tabari glosses it as not attending to Moses’ words and preserving them, from the sense of مراقبة as observing and keeping in view.

TABATABAI:20:92-94/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r5.claim: “Son of my mother” is contracted from “son of my mother” and is an appeal to kinship and affection meant to calm Moses' anger.
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r5.anchor: أصله يا ابن أمي وهى كلمة استرحام واسترآف قالها لإسكات غضب موسى

TABATABAI:20:92-94/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r6.claim: Aaron's plea indicates that Moses seized his beard and head in anger, apparently to strike him, as another verse states.
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r6.anchor: ويظهر من قوله { لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي } أنه أخذ بلحيته ورأسه غضبا ليضربه

TABATABAI:20:92-94/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r7.claim: Aaron's unstated condition is that forceful resistance would win only some followers, dividing Israel into obedient believers and disobedient idolaters and perhaps provoking fighting.
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r7.anchor: لو كنت مانعتهم عن عبادة العجل وقاومتهم بالغة ما بلغت لم يطعني إلا بعض القوم وأدى

TABATABAI:20:92-94/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r8.claim: Aaron says he feared Moses would judge that he had fractured Israel and ignored the order to reform them rather than follow the corrupters.
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r8.anchor: وقد كنت أمرتني بالإصلاح إذ قلت لي { أصلح ولا تتبع سبيل المفسدين } فخشيت أن تقول حين رجعت

TABATABAI:20:92-94/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r9.claim: Moses accepts Aaron's excuse and prays for Aaron and himself, as the account continues in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
TABATABAI:20:92-94/r9.anchor: هذا ما اعتذر به هارون وقد عذره موسى ودعا له ولنفسه كما في سورة الأعراف بقوله

THALABI:v1p89#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r1.speaker: علي ابن أبي طالب
THALABI:v1p89#2/r1.claim: Ali reports that al-Fatiha descended in Mecca from a treasure beneath the Throne; Thaʿlabī says this is the majority view.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r1.anchor: عن علي ابن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) قال: «نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة من كنز تحت العرش» . وعلى هذا أكثر العلماء.

THALABI:v1p89#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r2.speaker: عمر ابن شرحبيل
THALABI:v1p89#2/r2.claim: Umar ibn Sharhabil says al-Fatiha was the first revelation: Muhammad confided his experience to Khadija, went with Abu Bakr to Waraqa, and Gabriel taught him its opening.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r2.anchor: عن عمر ابن شرحبيل قال: إن أول ما نزل من القرآن الحمد لله رب العالمين

THALABI:v1p89#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p89#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Muhammad recited the opening of al-Fatiha in Mecca and Quraysh responded, “May God break your mouth.”
THALABI:v1p89#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة فقال: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين. فقالت قريش: دق الله فاك

THALABI:v1p89#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v1p89#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says al-Fatiha was revealed in Medina.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: «فاتحة الكتاب أنزلت في المدينة»

THALABI:v1p89#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r5.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p89#2/r5.claim: Hasan ibn al-Fadl rejects Mujahid’s Medina report as anomalous because Mujahid alone reports it and the scholars disagree.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن بن الفضل: لكل عالم هفوة، وهذه منكرة من مجاهد لأنه تفرد بها، والعلماء على خلافه.

THALABI:v1p89#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v1p89#2/r6.claim: Thaʿlabī says the sound report from the Prophet through Ubayy ibn Kaʿb calls al-Fatiha among the first revelations and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated verses.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r6.anchor: وصح الخبر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حديث أبي بن كعب أنها من: «أول ما نزل من القرآن» » وأنها: «السبع المثاني»

THALABI:v1p89#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p89#2/r7.claim: Thaʿlabī argues that al-Fatiha must be Meccan: al-Hijr is indisputably Meccan, and God had already bestowed the seven oft-repeated verses while Muhammad was in Mecca.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r7.anchor: وسورة الحجر مكية بلا اختلاف. ومعلوم أن الله تعالى لم يمتن عليه بإتيانه السبع المثاني وهو بمكة، ثم أنزلها بالمدينة

THALABI:v1p89#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p89#2/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p89#2/r8.claim: Thaʿlabī also rejects a Medinan date because it would mean Muhammad prayed in Mecca for ten years without al-Fatiha, which reason cannot accept.
THALABI:v1p89#2/r8.anchor: ولا يسعنا القول بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بمكة يصلي عشر [سنوات] بلا فاتحة الكتاب، هذا مما لا تقبله العقول.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī says Moses grasped Aaron’s hair with his right hand and his beard with his left.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r6.claim: The account of Moses grabbing Aaron is omitted here because another sūra mentions it; Aaron’s words themselves show Moses had taken hold of him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p503#2/r6.anchor: ولم يذكر هاهنا أخذه لذكره في سورة أخرى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r1.claim: Calling him “son of my mother” rather than of their father softens the appeal and seeks sympathy, in al-Kalbī’s explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r1.anchor: - {قال ابن أم} أضافه إلى الأم دون الأب ترقيقا واستعطافا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq reports a view that Aaron was Moses’s maternal brother but not his paternal brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (وقيل في هارون إنه لم يكن أخا موسى لأبيه وكان أخاه لأمه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r3.claim: The phrase is also read yā-bna-ummi with either kasra or fatḥa; the analysis was given at 7:150.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r4.claim: “By my head” means by the hair of my head.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي} أراد ولا شعر رأسي.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r5.claim: Grabbing the beard was not then considered humiliating; custom treated it like taking someone by the hand, and customs affect how acts are judged.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r5.anchor: أن العادة في ذلك الزمان لم تكن كهذه العادة بل كان يجري ذلك مجرى القبض على اليد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r6.claim: Another explanation is that Moses held Aaron’s beard as he might hold his own when angry, trusting Aaron as he trusted himself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r6.anchor: وقيل: (إنه أجراه مجرى نفسه إذا غضب في القبض على لحيته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says Moses thought Aaron had disobeyed God by not following him, so he seized Aaron in anger for God and to discipline him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p504/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: (وقع في نفس موسى أن هارون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Aaron’s fear as: if I had come to you, leaving the people behind, you would have accused me of dividing Israel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {إني خشيت} قال ابن عباس: (يريد إن أنا أتيتك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses Israel as the community; Aaron feared it would split into factions and fall into conflict and bloodshed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r2.anchor: {أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل} قال ابن عباس: (يريد (¬6): جماعتهم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r3.claim: Aaron’s excuse is a plausible judgment: some would follow Moses, some stay as believers opposing the calf, and some follow al-Sāmirī, risking violence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r3.anchor: فلا يؤمن أن يصيروا في الخلاف إلى تسافك، فاعتذر بما مثله يقبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r4.claim: Aaron had not kept Moses’s instruction to act as his deputy among the people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ولم ترقب قولي} يعني: ولم تحفظ وصيتي حين قلت لك: اخلفني في قومي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Aaron feared harshness would divide them into factions and make them kill one another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p505/r6.anchor: وقال في قوله: {خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل}: (خشيت من العنف بهم أن يتفرقوا أحزابا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r1.claim: Aaron feared that leaving the Israelites to follow Moses would divide them into factions that might kill each other, after which Moses would blame him for causing the division.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r1.anchor: خشيت إن فارقتهم واتبعتك أن يصيروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r2.claim: Aaron says Moses did not keep his charge to manage the Israelites well.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:94/r2.anchor: لم تحفظ وصيتي في حسن الخلافة عليهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p273/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p273/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p273/r7.claim: On returning and seeing the calf worship, Moses challenged Aaron and addressed him as his mother's son.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p273/r7.anchor: قال} [طه: 91-92] موسى لهارون لما رجع ورأى أنهم اتخذوا العجل. {يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا {92}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p274/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p274/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p274/r1.claim: Aaron feared Moses would say he divided Israel and did not heed his instruction.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p274/r1.anchor: {إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي} [طه: 94] قال: أي ولم

BAQILLANI:v1p279/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r1.claim: Speech from a fitting source and subject has a natural grandeur, whereas artificial imitation reveals estrangement and confusion.
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r1.anchor: والشيء إذا صدر من أهله وبدا من أصله وانتسب إلى ذويه سلم في نفسه وبانت فخامته

BAQILLANI:v1p279/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r2.claim: Abū Nuwās suits wine and drinking, while Dhū al-Rumma suits wilderness, camels, and pastoral life; Bāqillānī faults Abū Nuwās for treating ruins and wild animals.
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r2.anchor: نعرف في شعر أبي نواس أثر الشطارة وتمكن البطالة وموقع كلامه في وصف ما هو بسبيله

BAQILLANI:v1p279/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r3.claim: Abū Nuwās’ poem beginning with descriptions of ruined dwellings illustrates his poor fit for that subject, unlike his treatment of wine.
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r3.anchor: عيب أبي نواس التصرف في وصف الطلول والرباع والوحش

BAQILLANI:v1p279/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r4.speaker: براكوية الزنجاني
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r4.claim: Baraqawiyya al-Zanjānī recounts a poet reciting a ruin-themed poem to Hilāl ibn Yazīd on al-Aʿshā’s meter, then gives a quip about a young man from Zanjān mourning a ruin.
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r4.anchor: سمعت براكوية الزنجاني يقول أنشد بعض الشعراء هلال بن يزيد قصيدة على وزن قصيدة الأعشى

BAQILLANI:v1p279/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r5.claim: The examples show that each kind of expression has a proper source and domain, and its fit reveals the nature of what produced it.
BAQILLANI:v1p279/r5.anchor: وإنما ذكرت لك هذه الأمور لتعلم أن الشيء في معدنه أعز وإلى مظانه أحن وإلى أصله أنزع

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r1.claim: The book is deliberately concise because a full account of the Qurʾān’s qualities would be vast; even a brief exposition can indicate the method and guide readers to the proof.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r1.anchor: والذي سطرناه في الكتاب وإن كان موجزا وما أملينا فيه وإن كان خفيفا

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r2.claim: When a subject is exalted, excessive elaboration can become inept and description can fall short.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r2.anchor: متى عظم محل الشيء فقد يكون الإسهاب فيه عيا والإكثار في وصفه تقصيرا

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r3.speaker: الحكيم
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r3.claim: A sage says an orator becomes tongue-tied when describing passion or a beloved, illustrating how difficult eloquent description can be.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r3.anchor: قال الحكيم وقد سئل عن البليغ متى يكون عييا فقال متى وصف هوى أو حبيبا

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r4.speaker: أعرابي
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r4.claim: A lost Bedouin guided by moonlight hesitates whether to pray that the moon be raised, illuminated, or beautified, since each quality is already present.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r4.anchor: وضل أعرابي في سفر له ليلا وطلع القمر فاهتدى به فقال ما أقول لك

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r5.claim: People differ in intellect, understanding, and knowledge; rhetorical criticism is especially difficult because it depends on subtle, deep, and varied forms of expertise.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r5.anchor: ولولا أن العقول تختلف والأفهام تتباين والمعارف تتفاضل

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r6.speaker: المتنبي
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r6.claim: Al-Mutanabbī’s lines say that readers may blame a sound statement because of poor understanding and receive poetry according to their aptitude and learning.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r6.anchor: أنشدني أبو القاسم الزعفراني قال أنشدني المتنبي لنفسه القطعة التي يقول فيها

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r7.speaker: البحتري
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r7.claim: Al-Buḥturī’s poem says poetry can move people who would not feel a sword blow, while the poet cannot make fools understand his crafted verse.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r7.anchor: أنشدنا الحسن بن عبد الله قال أنشدني بعض مشايخنا للبحتري

BAQILLANI:v1p299/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r8.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r8.claim: Since judging all the varieties of human speech is difficult, assessing the speech of the Lord is more demanding still; those who count only ten forms of eloquence grasp little of it.
BAQILLANI:v1p299/r8.anchor: فإذا كان نقد الكلام كله صعبا وتمييزه شديدا والوقوع على اختلاف فنونه متعذرا وهذا في كلام الآدميين

BAQILLANI:v1p27/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r6.claim: Different responses to recitation do not refute its evidentiary force: hearers had distinct obstacles, including doubt about God, divine unity, or prophethood.
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r6.anchor: قيل له لا يجب ذلك لأن صوار فهم كانت كثيرة منها أنهم كانوا يشكون

BAQILLANI:v1p27/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r7.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r7.claim: At the conquest, Abū Sufyān professed that there is no god but God but admitted uncertainty about the Prophet’s messengership, illustrating one such obstacle.
BAQILLANI:v1p27/r7.anchor: ألا ترى أن أبا سفيان بن حرب لما جاء إلى رسول الله ليسلم عام الفتح

BURHAN:v1p422/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p422/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p422/r4.claim: Aaron first calls Moses ابن أم while close at hand; when Moses persists, يا ابن أم signals emotional distance and reaffirms their kinship, reflected in the connected written form.
BURHAN:v1p422/r4.anchor: لما أخذ موسى برأس أخيه اعتذر إليه فناداه من قرب على الأصل الظاهر فى الوجود ولما تمادى ناداه بحرف النداء

BURHAN:v2p250/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p250/r1.claim: The twenty-eighth address type is affectionate address, illustrated by Abraham’s gentle يا أبت, Luqman’s يا بني, and Aaron’s يا ابن أم.

BURHAN:v3p423#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r3.claim: The most forceful simile omits both the comparison’s aspect and particle; omitting only one yields the less emphatic forms illustrated by ‘Zayd is like a lion.’
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r3.anchor: أعلى مراتب التشبيه في الأبلغية ترك وجه الشبه وأداتة نحو زيد أسد

BURHAN:v3p423#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r4.speaker: صاحب المفتاح
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r4.claim: The author of al-Miftāḥ implies that dropping the aspect of comparison is more eloquent than dropping its particle because the aspect is more general.
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r4.anchor: وفي كلام صاحب المفتاح إشارة إلى أن ترك وجه الشبه أبلغ من ترك أداتة

BURHAN:v3p423#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r5.speaker: صاحب ضوء المصباح
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r5.claim: The author of Ḍawʾ al-Miṣbāḥ disagrees: a general omitted aspect may suggest blame rather than praise; the counterargument is that context can also direct an omitted particle toward praise.
BURHAN:v3p423#2/r5.anchor: وخالفه صاحب ضوء المصباح 1 لأنه إذا عم واحتمل التعدد

BURHAN:v2p463/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p463/r1.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v2p463/r1.claim: Sibawayh analyzes the expression يا هذا الحمد as apposition even though the demonstrative is more definite than the definite noun.
BURHAN:v2p463/r1.anchor: وقال سيبويه جعل ياهذا الحمد عطف بيان مع ان اسم الاشارة اعرف من المضاف إلى ذي اللام

ITQAN:v3p92/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.claim: An affectionate address appears in Abraham's gentle address to his father, Luqmān's address to his son, and Aaron's appeal to Moses; 20:94 is cited as an example.
ITQAN:v3p92/r2.anchor: الحادي والثلاثون خطاب التحبب نحو ﴿ يا أبت لم تعبد ﴾ ﴿ يا بني إنها إن تك ﴾

ITQAN:v4p451/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p451/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p451/r1.claim: In joined orthography, يوم هم, لات حين, and ابن أم are written together; in Ṭā Hā the hamza is written as wāw and the hamza of ابن is omitted, yielding يبنؤم.
ITQAN:v4p451/r1.anchor: و ( يوم هم ) و ( لات حين ) و ( ابن أم ) إلا في طه فكتبت الهمزة حينئذ واوا

ITQAN:v3p245/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p245/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p245/r5.claim: Jinas al-qalb reverses the order of letters, illustrated by farraqt between the Children of Israel.
ITQAN:v3p245/r5.anchor: ومنها تجنيس القلب بأن يختلفا في ترتيب الحروف نحو ﴿ فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ﴾

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r1.claim: A simile drawn from a continually seen image is familiar and commonplace; one drawn from a rarely seen image is novel and striking, with intermediate cases graded between these extremes.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r1.anchor: كل شبه رجع إلى وصف أو صورة أو هيئة من شأنها أن ترى وتبصر أبدا فالتشبيه المعقود عليه نازل مبتذل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r2.claim: ‘Separation’ in description means examining multiple features individually; one form isolates some features and omits others, as in separating smoke from a flame’s light or depicting eyes without lids.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p143/r2.anchor: اعلم أن قولنا التفصيل عبارة جامعة ومحصولها على الجملة أن معك وصفين أو أوصافا فأنت تنظر فيها واحدا واحدا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r1.claim: A paired simile is not truly composite when it only places two independent comparisons together: raw and dried bird-hearts resemble jujubes and old dates, and each comparison survives separation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r1.anchor: كأن قلوب الطير رطبا ويابسا لدى وكرها العناب والحشف البالى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r2.claim: In a genuine composite simile, one image can lose its point when detached from the other; the night-as-cover comparison is ineffective when isolated from its paired element.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r2.anchor: أن الجلال في قوله كطرف أشهب ملقى الجلال في مقابلة الليل وأنت لو قلت كأن الليل جلال وسكت لم يكن شيئا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r3.claim: The stars-as-pearls and sky-as-blue-carpet comparisons work separately, but combining them creates the startling spectacle of scattered, glinting stars against blue that the divided similes lose.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p168/r3.anchor: وكأن أجرام النجوم لوامعا درر نثرن على بساط أزرق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r1.claim: A compound simile depends on the whole arrangement: Mars looks like a person escaping at night because Jupiter appears before it like a candle, so Mars cannot be interpreted alone.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r1.anchor: كأنما المريخ والمشتري قدامه في شامخ الرفعة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r2.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s cup and mouth together resemble a crescent disappearing into twilight; neither isolated likeness conveys the intended image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r2.anchor: كأنه وكأن الكأس في فمه هلال أول شهر غاب في شفق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو الحسن
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī Abū al-Ḥasan says reversing the color order would fully capture beauty: a blushing cheek has white encircling red, though the poet may have followed the rose’s opposite arrangement.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r3.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو الحسن رحمه الله لو أتفق له أن يقول احمرار في جوانبه بياض لكان قد أستوفى الحسن

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r4.claim: Splitting the white-and-red comparison erases its beauty: white alone offers no meaningful simile, while the joined color arrangement creates the effect.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p171/r4.anchor: فأنظر الآن إن فرقت كيف يتفرق عنك الحسن والإحسان ويحضر العى ويذهب البيان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r1.speaker: الجميع
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r1.claim: The commentators treat Abū al-Najm’s nominative كل as an unnecessary poetic license, arguing that accusative would preserve meter and intended sense.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r1.anchor: قد حمله الجميع على أنه أدخل نفسه من رفع ' كل ' في شيء ، إنما يجوز عند الضرورة من غير أن كانت به ضرورة .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r2.claim: Al-Jurjānī rejects that account: the nominative is deliberate because it means the speaker committed none of the alleged sin, whereas accusative would imply he committed some of it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r2.anchor: وإذا تأملت وجدتَه لم يرتكبه ، ولم يحمل نفسه عليه إلا لحاجة له إلى ذلك ، وإلا لأنه رأى النصب يمنعه ما يريد .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r3.claim: With a negated verb, using كل means that some of the group or amount was encountered or taken while the remainder was not; it does not mean none at all.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r3.anchor: لا يصلح أن يكون إلا حيث يراد أن بعضا كان ، وبعضا لم يكن .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r4.claim: In affirmative statements, كل marks the full scope and blocks an inference that some people or items were left out; its force is emphatic rather than creating the scope from nothing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p215/r4.anchor: وإذا نظرت وجدته قد اجتلب لأن يفيد الشمول في الفعل الذي تسنده إلى الجملة أو توقعه بها .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p225/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p225/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p225/r1.claim: Knowledge is like a mine: the fact that a hundred loads of ore yielded gold should encourage one to search for even a tiny amount of learning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p225/r1.anchor: فكما أنه لا يمنعك أن ترى ألف وقر قد أخرجت من معدن تبر أن تطلب فيه ، وأن تأخذ ما تجد ولو كقدر تومة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r1.claim: A crafted object can be copied exactly in another instance, but a composed utterance cannot reproduce a poem’s or prose passage’s exact meaning and qualities through different wording.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r1.anchor: ليس يتصور مثل ذلك في الكلام ، لأنه لا سبيل إلى أن تجيء إلى معنى بيت من الشعر ، أو فصل من النثر فتؤديه بعينه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r2.claim: When people say a later wording gives the same meaning, they mean it achieves the same purpose, not that its precise sense and effect match the original.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p202/r2.anchor: والمراد أنه أدى الغرض ؛ فأما أن يؤدي المعنى بعينه على الوجه الذي يكون عليه في كلام الأول

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r1.speaker: دريد بن الصمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r1.claim: In Duraid’s line, ظنوا means be sure of the enemy’s arrival, not merely suspect it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r1.anchor: قال دريد بن الصمة : فقلت لهم: ظنوا بألفي مدجح

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p119/r8.claim: جلل can describe either great or small: each is large beside something smaller and small beside something larger.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r1.speaker: الحطيئة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r1.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa reverses the syntax: the hoof holds the rope, rather than the rope holding the hoof; each holds the other while attached.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r1.anchor: قال الحطيئة : فلما خشيت الهون والعير ممسك

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r2.speaker: الأخطل
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r2.claim: Al-Akhṭal reverses the roles; the intended sense is that the group’s backsides reached Najrān and Hajar, since what one reaches also reaches one.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r2.anchor: وقال الأخطل : على العيارات هداجون قد بلغت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r3.speaker: آخر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r3.claim: An anonymous poet puts الأفعوان and الشجاع in the accusative where the expected construction makes them nominative, since allies act on one another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r3.anchor: وقال آخر : قد سالم الحيات منه القدما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r4.speaker: الشماخ
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r4.claim: Al-Shammākh reverses agent and object in عصب العلباء بالعود; the expected order is عصب العود بالعلباء, though either construction is used.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r4.anchor: وقال الشماخ يذكر أباه : منه ولدت ولم يؤشب به حسبي

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r5.claim: Dhū al-Rummah reverses object and recipient: he means clothing the waist with a shield, since كسوت can take the garment or its wearer as object.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r5.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة : وتكسو المجن الرخو خصرا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r6.speaker: أبو النجم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r6.claim: Abū al-Najm reverses what approaches what: he means the constellation approaching the horizon, since each draws near to the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r6.anchor: وقال أبو النجم : قبل دنو الأفق من جوزائه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r7.speaker: الراعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r7.claim: Al-Rāʿī says hunters see the eye as a track, where the expected phrasing is that they see the track as clearly as an eye; the inversion is reciprocal.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r7.anchor: وقال الراعي يصف ثورا : فصبحته كلاب الغوث يوسدها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r8.speaker: النابغة
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r8.claim: Al-Nābigha reverses the comparison of fears; he means the antelope’s fear is no greater than his own, so their fears are equal.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p123/r8.anchor: وقال النابغة : وقد خفت حتى ما تزيد مخافتي

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r1.claim: Most readers use kasra in لِحية, which the author calls the eloquent form.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r1.anchor: والجمهور على كسر اللام من اللحية وهي الفصحى.

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r2.speaker: عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r2.claim: ʿIsa ibn Sulayman al-Hijazi reads the word with fatḥa, the Hijazi dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r2.anchor: وفيها الفتح. وبه قرأ عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي. والفتح لغة الحجاز.

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r3.claim: The plural is لحى, like قرب; a damma form is also transmitted, although صور is said with kasra where ḍamma would be expected.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r3.anchor: ويجمع على لحى كقرب,. ونقل فيها الضم، كما قالوا: صور بالكسر، وحقها الضم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r4.claim: The ب is not extra: it can mean 'do not let taking happen from you' or accompany an omitted object, 'do not seize me.'
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r4.anchor: والباء في " بلحيتي " ليست زائدة: إما لأن المعنى: لا يكن منك أخذ، وإما لأن المفعول محذوف أي: لا تأخذني.

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r5.claim: The author calls the claim that ب is extra, as in 2:195, an overreach.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r5.anchor: ومن زعم زيادتها كهي في ولا تلقوا بأيديكم [البقرة: 195] فقد تعسف.

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r6.claim: ولم ترقب قولي is accusative and coordinated with فرقت: Aaron feared Moses would say both that he split Israel and that he disregarded his word.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r6.anchor: قوله: { ولم ترقب قولي } هذه الجملة محلها النصب نسقا [على] { فرقت بين بني إسرآئيل } أي: أن تقول: فرقت بينهم، وأن تقول: لم ترقب قولي

SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads ترقب with ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from أرقب.
SAMIN-DURR:20:94/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر " ترقب " بضم حرف المضارعة من أرقب.

ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n79/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n79/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n79/r1.claim: Asad points to his note on 7:150 for the parallel account of Aaron's response.

ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r1.claim: Asad glosses the phrase as “my word” or “what I had said.”
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r1.anchor: "to my word" or "to what I had said"

ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r2.claim: Zamakhshari takes Aaron's prior instruction to concern the importance of keeping the Israelites united.
ASAD-NOTES:20:94#n80/r2.anchor: evidently, about the importance of keeping the people united (Zamakhshari)

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r1.claim: The Quran’s rhetorical inimitability is the majority position among speculative theologians; disagreement concerns whether other aspects of inimitability stand apart from its composition and eloquence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r1.anchor: ذهب إليه الأكثرون من علماء أهل النظر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r2.claim: Early works on Quranic inimitability by al-Khattabi, al-Rummani, and al-Baqillani resemble rhetorical studies, despite treating theologians’ views of the miracle.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r2.anchor: فرسائل الخطابي السني، والرماني المعتزلى، والباقلانى الأشعري تأخذ مكانها في المكتبة البلاغية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r3.speaker: الجرجاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r3.claim: Al-Jurjani presents his study of composition and rhetoric under the title Dalāʾil al-Iʿjāz.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r4.speaker: أبو هلال العسكري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r4.claim: Abu Hilal al-Askari ranks eloquence after knowledge of God because it reveals the Quran’s inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r4.anchor: أحق العلوم بالتعلم وأولاها بالحفظ، بعد المعرفة بالله جل ثناؤه، علم البلاغة والفصاحة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p94/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the sciences of bayān and maʿānī are necessary to grasp the Messenger’s miracle and the subtleties of his proof.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r1.claim: One cannot judge the rhetorical beauty of a text in a language without knowing that language’s expressive resources; Arabic eloquence is needed to recognize Quranic composition.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r1.anchor: فغير متصور أن يكون لمن أعوزته الدراية بأسرار التعبير في لغة ما، أن يقدر روائع نصوصها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r2.speaker: الباقلاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r2.claim: Al-Baqillani belittled celebrated poems and speeches, implying that Arabs accepted the Quran’s miracle despite low eloquence; the author rejects that portrayal.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r2.anchor: تورط فيه "الباقلاني" حين تعقب مشهور القصائد والخطب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r3.claim: The author argues the Arabs of the Prophet’s era were highly eloquent, which enabled them to recognize the Quran’s inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r3.anchor: أن يكونوا قد بلغوا من علو المستوى في الفصاحة والبلاغة، ما يجعلهم قادرين على إدراك هذا الإعجاز

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r4.claim: The author disagrees with al-Jurjani’s reliance on poetry and prose as the place to find Arabic rhetorical secrets; they should also be sought in the Quran, the highest text.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r4.anchor: لكنا نختلف مع الجرحاني، في أن تُلتمس أسرار البيان العربي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r5.claim: Al-Jurjani offers valuable rhetorical observations but no Quran-centered study of rhetorical inimitability; his work is preparatory to that subject.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r5.anchor: قدم ملاحظ دقيقة مما لمحه من أسرار البلاغة العربية، ولم يقدم دراسة قرآنية للإعجاز البلاغي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r6.claim: The author leaves open what in Quranic composition surpassed Arab eloquence and prevented the Arabs from producing a comparable sura.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p124/r6.anchor: ويظل السؤال قائماً: ما وجه فوت النظم القرآني نظم البلغاء من العرب؟ وماذا بهرهم من أسرار بيانه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r1.claim: Every sura opened by disjointed letters argues for the Quran’s divine origin and rebuts its opponents, while recalling earlier nations that rejected God’s signs and messengers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r1.anchor: ما من سورة بُدئت بالحروف المقطعة، إلا كان فيها احتجاج للقرآن وتقرير نزوله من عند الله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r2.claim: Most suras beginning with these letters came when polytheist opposition peaked; the Quran challenged them and their jinn allies to produce a sura, ten suras, or a comparable account, and they failed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r2.anchor: أكثر السور المبدوءة بالفواتح، نزلت في المرحلة التي بلغ فيها عتو المشركين أقصى المدى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r3.claim: The disconnected letters are Arabic letters familiar to the audience but meaningless in isolation; placed in the Quran, they disclose an inimitable expressive secret.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r3.anchor: تلك الحروف التي تقرأ مقطعة مفردة أو مركبة، فلا تعطي دلالة ما، لكنها حين تأخذ مكانها في القرآن يتجلى سرها البياني المعجز

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r4.claim: The same bare letters make human speech, reading, and knowledge possible, distinguishing humans from mute animals and enabling their responsibility as stewards on earth.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r4.anchor: ومنها تصاغ الكلمات فيحقق بها الإنسان آية نطقه وبيانه، ويحقق آية القراءة والعلم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r5.claim: The Quran’s miraculous eloquence consists of those same letters available in Arabic, yet the Arabs could not compose a sura like it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p180/r5.anchor: والحروف التي يتألف منها مبذولة لهم في لغتهم التي نزل بها القرآن كتاباً عربياً مبيناً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r1.claim: In al-Bukhārī’s Prophets chapter, Mujāhid explains the expression as “do not weaken us.”
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r1.anchor: في كتاب الأنبياء من صحيح البخاري عن مجاهد أيضاً: لا تضعفنا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وجمهور أهل التأويل
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most interpreters gloss it as “do not delay” or “do not slacken.”
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r2.anchor: أسنده الطبري عن ابن عباس وجمهور أهل التأويل بلفظه أو بلفظ لا تبطئا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd instead takes al-wānī to mean the heedless or languid person.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r3.anchor: لم يذكر خلافاً بينهم إلا ما أسنده عن ابن زيد قال: الواني الغافل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r4.speaker: أبان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r4.claim: Abān explains the form as “does not cease,” supported by Ṭarafa’s image of pots that never stop boiling.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r4.anchor: وفيه عن أبان، قال: لا ينى لا يزال

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r5.speaker: القرطبي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says al-wanā can convey weakness, sluggishness, languor, and exhaustion, all of which suit the passage.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r5.anchor: قال القرطبي: والونى الضعف والفتور والكلال والإعياء، وكله مراد في الآية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r6.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ prefers slackness, delay, and faltering resolve for “mā wanītu” over bare incapacity; Arabic distinguishes negligent languor from deliberate patience.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p335/r6.anchor: وفي الوني من دلالة الإبطاء والتقصير وفتور الهمة والعزيمة

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r1.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r1.claim: Al-Rifai credits Amin al-Khuli with launching religious-studies teaching at al-Azhar: in 1935 he began teaching History of Religions at the Faculty of Theology.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r1.anchor: في سنة ١٩٣٥م بدأ الخولي بتدريس «تاريخ المِلل والنحَل» في كلية أصول الدين في الأزهر

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r2.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r2.claim: Al-Rifai says Khuli trained students to study religions and their histories through modern scientific research, moving beyond reliance on old reports and narrations.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r2.anchor: تركز بحثُه على تعليم تلامذتِه كيفية دراسة الأديان وتاريخِها على وَفْق مناهج البحثِ العلمي الحديث، وعدم التوقف عند الأخبار والمرويات القديمة الواردة في دراستِها

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r3.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r3.claim: Khuli urged applying modern scientific knowledge to religion’s origins and nature, studying its fit with its society and the reciprocal ways religion and social conditions, culture, and adherents shape one another.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r3.anchor: نبه أمين الخولي تلامذتَه إلى ضرورةِ توظيف المُعطيات العلمية الحديثة في دراسة نشأة الدين، وبيان ماهيته، واكتشاف التنَاغُم بين الدين ونمط عيش وظروفِ وثقافة المجتمع

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r4.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r4.claim: Khuli argues that religious history needs wider material and immaterial evidence than transmitted reports; because religion permeates human life and its artistic, scientific, and practical forms, silent evidence should be sought as especially truthful.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r4.anchor: في بيانه لمنهجه هذا يكتب أمين الخولي: «إن دراسة تاريخ الأديان تحتاج إلى مصادر أوسع وأكثر من الرواية المنقولة والخبر المسرود

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r5.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r5.claim: Khuli endorses experimental historiography: modern researchers distrust reports, investigate artifacts and ruins, and decipher ancient languages; tangible evidence can err but is less vulnerable to bias, manipulation, and false testimony.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r5.anchor: أمين الخولي عن إعلان منهجِه الذي ينسج على منوال المنهج العلمي الجديد في دراسة الدين، واكتشاف نشأتِه ومسيرته عبر التاريخ في ضوء ما يسميه

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r6.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r6.claim: Al-Rifai says Khuli’s pioneering effort never became established: such projects remained individual and alien to inherited courses, whose closed structure they could not penetrate or rebuild.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r6.anchor: محاولة أمين الخولي الرائدة في توطين علم الأديان في الأزهر لم تترسخ ولم تأخذ نصابَها الذي تستحقه في إعادة بناء التعليم الديني

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r7.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r7.claim: Al-Rifai blames the expansion and institutional dominance of Salafism for extinguishing serious attempts to rebuild religious education in the Islamic world.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r7.anchor: وجاء تمدد التيار السلفي واكتساحُه لمؤسسات التعليم الديني ليقضي على كل المحاولات الجادة لإعادة بناء هذا التعليم في عالَم الإسلام ويجهضها في مهدها

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r8.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r8.claim: Al-Rifai says traditional schools’ curricula remain trapped in a self-repeating cycle despite periodic calls to renew religious education.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r8.anchor: ما زال الأزهر وغيره من مدارس العلم التقليدية في عالَم الإسلام تتردد فيها من حين لآخر دعواتٌ لتجديد النظام التعليمي، غير أن مقرراتها التعليمية ما زالت تدور في حلقة مفرغة لا تبدأ إلا حيث تنتهي ولا تنتهي إلا حيث تبدأ

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r9.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r9.claim: Al-Rifai says politicians and their preacher allies repeatedly call for curricular renewal, but political concern arose only after Salafism threatened their position.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r9.anchor: يقوله السياسيون ويكتبه وعاظُهم باستمرار، ولم يهتم السياسيون بذلك إلا بعد أن أضحت السلفية تهدد وجودَهم

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r10.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r10.claim: Al-Rifai judges these renewal efforts to be superficial patchwork that stays on the surface and fails to reshape religious education’s underlying structure.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r10.anchor: إلا أن هذه الدعوات لم تنتج إلا محاولات شكلية ترقيعية، تمكث عند السطح، وتفشل في التوغل داخل البنية العميقة للتعليمِ الديني كي تعيد تشكيلَها

RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r11.claim: Al-Rifai attributes failure to weak engagement with modernity: serious reform requires understanding contemporary sciences, applying them to religion and its texts for Muslims’ present needs, and critically sifting and dismantling inherited tradition.
RIFAI-KHULI:c3/r11.anchor: وتعود أسباب فشل هذه الدعوات إلى أنها لم تدرك بعد أن كل عملية إعادة بناءٍ جادةٍ تتطلب وعيًا بالعصر واستيعابًا لمنطق علومِه وإتقانًا للغةِ معارفِه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r1.claim: The concise account in al-Aʿrāf omits the vocative particle where meaning stays clear, while Ṭāhā’s fuller narration includes it as part of its detailed wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r1.anchor: عندما يكون السياق في مقام البسط والتفصيل يذكر الحرف سواء كان ياء أو غيرها من الأحرف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p772/r2.claim: Including a particle can also serve emphasis, in addition to marking a detailed context.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p771/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p771/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p771/r4.claim: He poses but does not answer the question of why al-A'raf retains يا in ابن أم while Taha omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p771/r4.anchor: ما دلالة ذكر وحذف (يا) في قوله تعالى (ابن أوم) في سورة الأعراف و (يبنؤم) في سورة طه؟

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p743/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p743/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p743/r1.claim: In a preceding, unidentified comparison, he says the second wording is more emphatic: justice is general while the first case is very specific, explaining why على is omitted first and stated second.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p743/r1.anchor: الثانية آكد من الأولى؛ والأمر بالعدل أمر عام والأولى أمر خاص جداً لذا اقتضى حذف الحرف (على) في الأولى وذكره في الثانية

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.claim: In context, Moses was given signs to confront Pharaoh, not yet-revealed scripture: his tablets came after leaving Egypt, so his challenge used miracles such as the staff and hand; Jesus likewise challenged through signs, and these are the two cases described this way.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1030/r1.anchor: الأمر كان يتعلق بالإيتاء وليس بالإنزال بالنسبة لموسى يتعلق بالمعجزة كالعصا واليد في تسع آيات

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, and Hafs from Asim read yā ibn umma with fatḥa on the mīm.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ يابن أم بنصب الميم ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r2.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r2.claim: Abu Bakr from Asim, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Ibn Amir read the mīm with kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر وحمزة والكسائي وابن عامر (يا ابن أم) بكسر الميم.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r3.claim: With fatḥa, one analysis is vocative yā ibn ammā: the final alif and possessive yāʾ are deleted as in yā ghulām; alternatively ibn and umm form a compound built on fatḥa like khamsata ʿashara.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: من قال: يا ابن أم احتمل قوله أمرين: أحدهما: أن يكون أراد: يا ابن أما، فحذف الألف كما يحذف من غلامي في النداء إذا قال: يا غلام،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r4.claim: With kasra, one analysis makes ibn possessive to umm with the possessive yāʾ omitted; alternatively the two words form a compound attached to the speaker, with yāʾ deleted as in a singular vocative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p247#2/r4.anchor: ومن قال: (يا ابن أم) احتمل أمرين: أحدهما: أن يكون أضاف ابنا إلى أم، وحذف الياء من الثاني،

NASHR:v2p337/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p337/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p337/r6.claim: Al-Dānī says the writing of يا ابن أم omits both alifs, but the author saw Syrian, Egyptian, and Medinan codices retaining one; al-Dānī may have seen copies omitting both.
NASHR:v2p337/r6.anchor: أما ياابن أم، فقد قدمت في باب وقف حمزة أني رأيته في المصاحف الشامية من الجامع الأموي

QIRAAT-ER:20:94:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:4#1/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:4#1/r1.claim: Kasra rather than fatḥa on mīm makes the genitive inflection explicit in the construct form.
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:4#1/r1.anchor: Kasra on mīm instead of fatḥa — genitive inflection explicit; standard construct reading in many qira'at

QIRAAT-ER:20:94:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:12#1/r1.speaker: Y-iḍ
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:12#1/r1.claim: The variant adds yāʾ with iḍāfa, explicitly marking possession in the pronoun suffix.
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:12#1/r1.anchor: Added yāʾ with iḍāfa — explicit possessive marker; canonical variant extending the pronoun suffix

QIRAAT-ER:20:94:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:20#1/r1.speaker: HzT
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:20#1/r1.claim: This ten-reader form varies the orthographic handling of the hamza-alif sequence in Isrāʾīl.
QIRAAT-ER:20:94:20#1/r1.anchor: Variant hamza treatment — different orthographic handling of the hamza-alif sequence; in 10-reader canon

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: ليس خلق الله مثله requires an implicit pronoun; without it, the verb would have no noun to govern, as in إنه.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: In وليس كل النوى تلقى المساكين, كل is accusative under تلقى with an implicit subject after ليس; if governed by ليس it would be nominative.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: The line إذا مت كان الناس صنفان also contains an omitted pronoun, an instance of the same construction.

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: Some say كان أنت حير منه, construing it as if an initial إنه preceded أنت.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان أنت حير منه

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: The near-verb كاد allows the same ellipsis: كاد تزيغ means كادت قلوب فريق منهم تزيغ.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: ما كان الطيب إلا المسك is acceptable on the Tamimi analysis because it means ما الطيب إلا المسك.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: ما كان الطيب إلا المسك على إعمال ما كان

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: This ellipsis is unavailable with Hijazi ما, which does not license an implicit pronoun.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: Hijazi ما does not permit advancing a noun governed by a later predicate, as in ما زيدا عبد الله ضاربا or ما زيدا أنا قاتلا.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: With a nominative predicate, the Tamimi pattern أما زيدا فأنا ضارب works as if أما were absent, leaving زيدا as the object of ضارب.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.claim: Omitting the object pronoun in عارفه is preferable to rearrangement; speakers often omit this hāʾ, unlike the rare inversion.
SIBAWAYH:إذاقلتإنهمنيأتنانأتهوإنهأمةالله.anchor: إذا قلت إنه من يأتنا نأته وإنه أمة الله ذاهبة

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: In interrogatives, ذا functions like the relative الذي only with ما or interrogative من.
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.anchor: وليس يكون كالذي إلا مع ما ومن في الاستفهام فيكون ذا بمنزلة الذي

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: On the relative analysis of ماذا رأيت, ذا means الذي and the answer can be متاع حسن; Labid's verse supplies an example.

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: Alternatively, ما and ذا form one interrogative noun; ماذا رأيت can be answered خيرا, understood as ما رأيت خير, with accusative matching the question.

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: The Qur'anic answer خيرا and idiom عماذا تسأل show that ما وذا can form one interrogative name; otherwise Arabs would say عم ذا تسأل.

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: This fused analysis resembles combinations such as إنما، كأنما, and حينما, where elements behave as one expression.
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.anchor: وليس يكون كالذي إلا مع ما ومن في الاستفهام

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: The Qur'anic response أساطير الأولين is accusative under the fused analysis; a strict relative analysis would call for nominative خير.
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.anchor: ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: The reported line دعى ماذا علمت shows that the relative reading cannot simply be imposed wherever ماذا occurs.
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.anchor: وليس يكون كالذي إلا مع ما ومن في الاستفهام فيكون ذا بمنزلة الذي

SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.claim: Short answers like صالح to كيف أصبحت and زيد to من رأيت are understood through an omitted clause; an understood verb can also license accusative after من الذي رأيت.
SIBAWAYH:وليسيكونكالذيإلامعماومنفيالاستف.anchor: ومثل ذلك قولهم في جواب كيف أصبحت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r1.claim: Light أن in contexts of certainty takes an indicative clause, as if it were heavy أنه; the knowledge statement in 73:20 illustrates this.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r1.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r2.claim: The light أن in أفلا يرون أن لا يرجع إليهم قولا is also followed by an indicative because the clause expresses an asserted fact.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r3.claim: In لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب, أن لا يقدرون is indicative; Abī's codex reportedly reads أنهم لا يقدرون, supporting the heavy-clause analysis.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r4.claim: The أن that governs subjunctive verbs does not occur in a context of certainty and assertion.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r4.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r5.claim: After كتبت إليه أن لا, jussive marks a command, subjunctive marks purpose, and indicative reports that the addressee does not do it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r5.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r6.claim: Verbs of supposition ظننت، حسبت، خلت, and رأيت allow either light أن with subjunctive or heavy أن with indicative.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r6.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r7.claim: خشيت normally takes subjunctive because it does not assert an event as established, unlike supposition verbs; the same applies to أرجو، أطمع, and عسى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r7.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r8.claim: If خشيت concerns an event already established as certain, indicative is possible, though it is not the usual construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r8.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r9.claim: قد علمت أن تفعل and قد علمت أن فعل are weak without a future, perfect, or negation marker; these compensate for dropped أنه.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r9.anchor: هذا باب آخر أن فيه مخففة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r10.claim: The optative أما أن جزاك الله خيرا is allowed without قد or س because it is a prayer; common omission also supports أما إن جزاك الله خيرا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r10.anchor: وأما قولهم أما أن جزاك الله خيرا فإنهم إنما أجازوه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r11.claim: ما علمت إلا أن تقوم can suggest action without asserting it; a certain future is expressed as ما علمت إلا أن ستقومون.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r11.anchor: وتقول ما علمت إلا أن تقوم وما أعلم إلا أن تأتيه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r12.claim: Light أن is acceptable before a nominal predicate, as in قد علمت أن عمرو ذاهب, because that could also follow heavy أن.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابآخرأنفيهمخففة)#512/r12.anchor: وإنما جاز قد علمت أن عمرو ذاهب لأنك قد جئت بعده باسم وخبر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: A nominative ending has four pause forms: ishmām, plain silence, rawm (approximating the vowel), or consonant doubling.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: فأما المرفوع والمضموم فإنه يوقف عنده على أربعة أوجه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Ishmām distinguishes an ending mobile in connected speech from one always silent; plain pause treats both alike because both are silent there.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: آخر الكلم المتحركة في الوصل التي لا تلحقها زيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Rawm and doubling stress that the ending is normally mobile; doubling is strongest because it requires the following consonant to be vocalized.
