SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: آخر الكلم المتحركة في الوصل التي لا تلحقها زيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Sībawayh records notation for the forms: a dot for ishmām, khāʾ for plain silence, a line for rawm, and shīn for doubling.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: فللإشمام نقطة وللذي أجري مجرى الجزم والإسكان الخاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Al-Khalil and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb report Arab rawm; al-Khalil also reports pause without ishmām and with plain silence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: حدثنا بذلك عن العرب الخليل وأبو الخطاب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Poets add yāʾ, wāw, or alif in rhyme to reflect doubling at pause; examples include سبسبا and عيهل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: ومن ثم قالت العرب في الشعر في القوافي سبسبا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Ruʾba's rhyme جدبا represents جدب, and his الأضخما represents الأضخم, illustrating added alif in the poetic rhyme practice.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: They do not double when the penultimate consonant is already silent, as in عمرو and زيد; rawm or ishmām may still distinguish the ending.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: فإن كان الحرف الذي قبل آخر حرف ساكنا لم يضعفوا نحو عمرو وزيد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: In accusative and genitive forms speakers use rawm, doubling, or plain silence, but not ishmām, which depends on the nominative ḍamma.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: آخر الكلم المتحركة في الوصل التي لا تلحقها زيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: Ishmām is visible lip-rounding rather than audible sound, so an unseeing listener cannot distinguish it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: آخر الكلم المتحركة في الوصل التي لا تلحقها زيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.claim: A trusted informant heard an Arab say أعطني أبيضه, adding hāʾ to أبيض at pause by analogy with هنه while intending هن.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالوقففيms754آخرالكلمالمت.anchor: آخر الكلم المتحركة في الوصل التي لا تلحقها زيادة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: A five-letter noun ending in alif deletes that alif in nisba: حبارى becomes حباري, as do جمادى and قرقرى.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: تقول في حبارى حباري وفي جمادى جمادي وفي قرقرى قرقري

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Yunus treats مرامى as having an added alif and would form مراموي, by analogy with حبلى becoming حبلوي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Sībawayh rejects the overextended analogy because it predicts forms such as مقلولوي, whereas speakers say مقلولي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Deletion is good at the fourth position by analogy with extra alifs; at five or more letters it is required, and greater heaviness strengthens the requirement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Mamdūd nouns retain the final hamza in nisba regardless of length or declension because its case-vowel mobility makes it strong.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: The maqṣūr alif is weak because it takes no case endings, so it is deleted; a quiescent yāʾ can likewise drop, unlike a moving one.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: The nisba yāʾ compensates for a deleted weak ending; the alif alternates with the nisba yāʾ as hāʾ alternates in الجحاجحة and الجحاجيح.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: فإنما جعلوا ياءي الإضافة عوضا وهذه الألف أضعف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Nisba on عثير or حثيل follows the pattern of حميري.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Yunus groups مثنى with معزى and معطى as five-letter nouns like مرامى, implying the same deletion behavior.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: Sībawayh challenges Yunus because his analysis predicts عبدوي and would wrongly count a doubled consonant as one for declension.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.speaker: بعض العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.claim: For declinable حراء, some Arabs say حراوي and others preserve the hamza in حراني.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإضافةإلىكلاسمكانآخرهأل.anchor: هذا باب الإضافة إلى كل اسم كان آخره ألفا وكان على خمسة أحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r1.claim: Moses adds the mother in address to soften Aaron's heart, not because they were maternal half-brothers; the majority says they were full brothers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r1.anchor: خص الأم بالإضافة استعطافا وترقيقا لقلبه لا لما قيل من أنه كان أخاه لأمه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r2.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يا بن أم with a kasra on the mīm.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( يا بن أم ) بكسر الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r3.claim: The head refers to its hair, which is more naturally seized; al-Alusi says the familiar sense of beard is the hair growing on the chin.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r3.anchor: أي بشعر رأسي فإن الأخذ أنسب به وزعم بعضهم أن قوله ( بلحيتي ) على معنى بشعر لحيتي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r4.claim: A report says Moses seized Aaron's head hair with his right hand and beard with his left; al-Alusi says the wording and reports show that he did grasp his beard.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r4.anchor: روى أنه أخذ شعر رأسه بيمينه وليحيته بشماله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r5.claim: Moses was rigid and angry for God, believing Aaron's lapse warranted discipline, yet without removing him from prophetic infallibility; al-Alusi sees no legal objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r5.anchor: وكان عليه السلام حديدا متصلبا غضوبا لله تعالى وقد شاهد ما شاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r6.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r6.claim: Al-Razi argues that anger either removes reason, which Muslims cannot believe, or leaves the infallibility problem; al-Alusi finds his reply unhelpful.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r6.anchor: فقال : لا يخلو الغضب من أن يزيل عقله أولا والأول لا يعتقده مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r7.speaker: عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r7.claim: ʿĪsā ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥijāzī reads بلحيتي with fatḥa on the lām, a Hijazi dialect form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r7.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن سليمان الحجازي ( بلحيتي ) بفتح اللام وهي لغة أهل الحجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r8.claim: Aaron feared that fighting the rebels would make Israelites destroy one another and divide, or that joining Moses with the believers would provoke battle.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r8.anchor: أي خشيت لو قاتلت بعضهم ببعض وتفانوا وتفرقوا أو خشيت لو لحقتك بمن آمن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r9.claim: Calling them Children of Israel evokes their shared descent and unity; division follows naturally from fighting or Aaron's joining Moses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r9.anchor: مع كونه أبناء واحد كما ينبئ عن ذلك ذكرهم بهذا العنوان دون القوم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r10.claim: Another gloss takes division to mean the lasting fragmentation after fighting, with no hope of reunion.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r11.claim: Lam tarqub means that Aaron did not observe or respect Moses' instruction.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r12.claim: The final clause can coordinate with فَرَّقْتَ, making two feared accusations, or be a circumstantial clause: you divided them without awaiting my instruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r12.anchor: والجملة عطف على ( فرقت ) أي خشيت أن تقول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r13.claim: Moses' instruction was اخلفني في قومي وأصلح, and Aaron says he preserved the people through restraint and diplomacy until Moses returned.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r13.anchor: وأراد بقول موسى المضاف إلى الياء قوله عليه السلام : ( اخلفني في قومي وأصلح )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r14.claim: Aaron restrained the people without disrupting order or unity or provoking Moses' blame, especially because they had weakened him and nearly killed him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p251/r14.anchor: ولا يكون سببا للومك إياي إلى أن ترجع إليهم فتكون أنت المتدارك للأمر حسبما تراه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r1.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir transmits from Ibn Jurayj a view that the omitted saying is Aaron's own; the final clause is circumstantial, meaning he spoke without awaiting Aaron's words and clarification.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عب ابن جريج ما يدل أن المراد من القول المضاف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads ولم ترقب with ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on qāf, as the imperfect of أرقب.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p252/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ( ولم ترقب ) بضم التاء وكسر القاف مضارع أرقب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r4.claim: Moses had seized Aaron’s beard and head hair, specifically his forelocks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r4.anchor: أي بشعر رأسي وكان قد أخذ ذوائبه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r5.claim: Aaron feared that objecting would divide the Israelites into factions that fought one another, and Moses would blame him for splitting them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r5.anchor: لو أنكرت عليهم لصاروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r6.claim: Aaron says he feared Moses would say he had not kept the instruction to remain among the people and treat them gently.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p291/r6.anchor: حين قلت لك اخلفني في قومي، وأصلح أي ارفق بهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r6.claim: Aaron invokes their mother rather than their father to soften Moses; it is also said they shared only a mother, while the majority say they shared both parents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r6.anchor: خص الأم استعطافا وترقيقا، وقيل لأنه كان أخاه من الأم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r7.speaker: الجمهور
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r7.claim: The majority hold that Aaron and Moses were full brothers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r7.anchor: والجمهور على أنهما كانا من أب وأم

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r8.claim: Moses seized Aaron by his beard and head hair, overcome with fierce anger for God when he saw the calf worship; he was naturally stern and forceful.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r8.anchor: أي بشعر رأسي قبض عليهما يجره إليه من شدة غيظه وفرط غضبه لله

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r9.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel if he fought the calf worshippers or split the people into factions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r9.anchor: لو قاتلت أو فارقت بعضهم ببعض

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r10.claim: Aaron did not disregard Moses' instruction to succeed him and set things right; reform meant preserving and accommodating the masses until Moses returned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:91-94/r10.anchor: حين قلت { اخلفني في قومي وأصلح } فإن الإصلاح كان في حفظ الدهماء

BINTSHATI:v1p14/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r1.claim: Few university Arabic professors have made Qur’anic text a subject of systematic study comparable to their study of other texts, despite its unsurpassed rhetoric.
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r1.anchor: من حاول أن يجعل من النص القرآني موضوعا لدراسة منهجية

BINTSHATI:v1p14/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r2.claim: Her survey of Arabic department examinations over a quarter-century found no question on Qur’anic rhetoric, showing that the idea had not taken root clearly enough.
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r2.anchor: فلم أجد من بينها سؤالا في البيان القرآني، فدل هذا على أن الفكرة لم تأخذ حظها الكافي من الوضوح

BINTSHATI:v1p14/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r3.claim: Qur’anic studies broadly lack a method and are sometimes undertaken by authors unqualified for them.
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r3.anchor: والدراسات القرآنية، في المجال العام، تسير على غير منهج، ويتصدى لها من المؤلفين من ليسوا أهلا لها

BINTSHATI:v1p14/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r4.claim: She recalls Muṣṭafā Ṣādiq al-Rāfiʿī’s work on the Qur’an’s inimitability and says its value is discussed in her book’s introduction on rhetorical inimitability.
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r4.anchor: في إعجاز القرآن، والحديث عن قيمتها يأتي في مدخل كتابي

BINTSHATI:v1p14/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r5.claim: Though she grew up listening to and reciting the Qur’an reverently, she came to grasp its rhetoric only through specialized study of texts and Arabic literary heritage, which made her question her earlier understanding of Arabic.
BINTSHATI:v1p14/r5.anchor: ألفت منذ الصغر أن أصغي بكل وجداني إلى هذا القرآن، وأن أتلو آياته في تأثر وخشوع، لكني لم أع بيانه حق الوعي

BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r18.claim: Harun appeals to their shared mother to soften Moses, although they were full brothers, because a mother is more tender and shares her child’s pain.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r18.anchor: فذكره بها خاصة وإن كان شقيقه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r19.claim: Harun’s head means the hair of his head.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r19.anchor: تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي } أي بشعره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r20.claim: Harun feared that forceful confrontation would be fruitless with few weak supporters and would divide Israel through deaths and kin retaliation.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r20.anchor: بفعلك هذا الذي لم يجد شيئا لقلة من كان معك وضعفكم عن ردهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r21.claim: Harun understood Moses’ instruction to make things right and avoid the corruptors, but not as an order to fight the dissenters even with the sword.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r21.anchor: ولم تقل وارددهم ولو أدى الأمر إلى السيف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r22.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r22.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r22.claim: The author compares Harun’s restraint under weak support to Muhammad’s instruction to use pardon, patience, and gentle resistance when allies were few.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p39#2/r22.anchor: كما كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مأمورا بالصفح والحلم

DURR-FULL:v5p595/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of splitting Israel because some people might follow Aaron while others stayed behind.
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r2.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل} قال: خشيت أن يتبعني بعضهم ويتخلف بعضهم

DURR-FULL:v5p595/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r3.claim: Qatāda adds that righteous people before the Israelites also disliked division.
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي اله عنه في قوله: {إني خشيت أن تقول فرقت بين بني إسرائيل} قال: قد كره الصالحون الفرقة قبلكم

DURR-FULL:v5p595/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains “you did not heed my word” as not waiting to see what Moses would do or say.
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله: {ولم ترقب قولي} قال: لم تنتظر قولي وما أنا صانع وقائل

DURR-FULL:v5p595/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as “you did not preserve my instruction.”
DURR-FULL:v5p595/r5.anchor: قال: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {ولم ترقب قولي} لم تحفظ قولي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r9.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r9.claim: These readers give yabnaʾumm; it can be yā ibn ammā with alif dropped for ease, or a compound indeclinable name like khamsata ʿashar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم «يبنؤم» يحتمل أن يريد يا بن أما فحذف الألف تخفيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r10.speaker: ابن كثير عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r10.claim: These readers give yā bin umm with kasra, explained as dropping yāʾ for ease; alternatively the words form a compound whose possessive yāʾ is omitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير عن عاصم وحمزة والكسائي «يا بن أم» بالكسر على حذف الياء تخفيفا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the kasra reading irregular because this yāʾ differs from the deletable yāʾ in vocative forms such as yā ghulāmī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r11.anchor: وهو شاذ لأنها ليست كالياء في قولك يا غلامي وإنما هي كالياء في قولك يا غلام غلامي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r12.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r12.claim: A group says Hārūn and Moses shared only a mother; Ibn Atiyya calls this weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r12.anchor: وقالت فرقة لم يكن هارون أخا موسى إلا من أمه ع وهذا ضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r13.claim: Another group says they were full brothers; Hārūn invoked their mother to appeal more strongly to Moses’ compassion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة كان شقيقه وإنما دعاه بالأم لأن التداعي بالأم أشفق وأشد استرحاما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r14.claim: Moses angrily seized Hārūn by the beard; Moses is described as stern in temperament.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p60/r14.anchor: وأخذ موسى عليه السلام بلحية هارون غضبا وكان حديد الخلق عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r1.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ advises the people of Kufa to let the Quran guide them toward moderation and ease and away from injustice and hardship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r1.anchor: أبي الدرداء: إن إخوانا لك من أهل الكوفة يقرئونك السلام ويأمرونك أن توصيهم، فقال: أقرئهم السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd advises listening closely to each Quranic address to believers, since it contains either a command to good or a prohibition of evil.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r2.anchor: وقال رجل لعبد الله بن مسعود: أوصني، فقال: إذا سمعت الله تعالى يقول يا أيها الذين آمنوا فأرعها سمعك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r3.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said the best reciter is one whose recitation makes the listener recognize his fear of God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r3.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل عن أحسن الناس قراءة أو صوتا بالقرآن، فقال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r4.speaker: عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r4.claim: The Prophet urges people to recite before some make a display of Quranic performance while neglecting its meanings and seeking immediate reward.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r4.anchor: وقال عليه السلام: «اقرؤوا القرآن قبل أن يجيء قوم يقيمونه كما يقام القدح ويضيعون معانيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r5.claim: When Yemenis wept on first hearing the Quran during Abū Bakr’s caliphate, he said that they had once been similarly tender before their hearts hardened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r5.anchor: ويروى أن أهل اليمن لما قدموا أيام أبي بكر الصديق- رضي الله عنه- سمعوا القرآن فجعلوا يبكون فقال أبو بكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r6.claim: ʿUmar groaned on reciting the warning that his Lord’s punishment would surely come, and the effect lasted twenty days.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r6.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قرأ مرة: إن عذاب ربك لواقع، ما له من دافع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r7.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan criticizes people for turning Quran recitation into a nighttime journey through passages; earlier believers pondered God’s messages at night and acted on them by day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن البصري: إنكم اتخذتم قراءة القرآن مراحل، وجعلتم الليل جملا تركبونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says people were given the Quran to act upon it, yet some recite every letter while failing to practice it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r8.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه يقول: «أنزل عليهم القرآن ليعملوا به فاتخذوا درسه عملا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r9.claim: The author links the Quran’s accessibility to God’s repeated statement that He made it easy to remember and heed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r9.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: قال الله تعالى: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r10.claim: The “weighty word” includes understanding the Quran, acting on it, and fulfilling its obligations; people choose what is easy and abandon the demanded hard work.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r10.anchor: وقال تعالى: إنا سنلقي عليك قولا ثقيلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r11.speaker: يوسف بن أسباط
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r11.claim: Yūsuf ibn Asbāṭ says he seeks forgiveness after completing the Quran because recalling its duties makes him fear blame, so he turns to repentance and glorification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p38/r11.anchor: وقيل ليوسف بن أسباط: بأي شيء تدعو إذا ختمت القرآن؟ قال: «أستغفر الله من تلاوتي لأني

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r1.claim: On returning and seeing the grave event among his people, Moses became furious, dropped the divine tablets, and seized and dragged Aaron by the head; Ibn Kathir says the fuller account is in al-A'raf and invokes “news is not like seeing.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r1.anchor: يقول مخبرا عن موسى، عليه السلام، حين رجع إلى قومه، فرأى ما قد حدث فيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r4.claim: Although Moses and Aaron were full brothers, invoking their mother was gentler and more emotionally affecting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r4.anchor: مع أنه شقيقه لأبويه؛ لأن ذكر الأم هاهنا أرق وأبلغ، أي: في الحنو والعطف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r5.claim: Aaron explains that he feared following Moses to report the crisis would prompt Moses to accuse him of leaving the Israelites divided and alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r5.anchor: هذا اعتذار من هارون عند موسى في سبب تأخره عنه، حيث لم يلحقه فيخبره بما كان من هذا الخطب الجسيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r6.claim: “You did not heed my word” means Aaron would have failed to observe Moses's instruction when entrusted with the people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r6.anchor: أي: وما راعيت ما أمرتك به حيث استخلفتك فيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Aaron stood in awe of Moses and was obedient to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p312#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وكان هارون هائبا له مطيعا

JISHUMI:v7p4705/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4705/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4705/r4.claim: The bāʾ in bi-junūdihi is an extra particle for emphasis, as in lā taʾkhudh biliḥyatī and asrā biʿabdihi.
JISHUMI:v7p4705/r4.anchor: والباء في قوله: (بجنوده) صلة وتفخيم، كقوله: (لا تأخذ بلحيتي) (أسرى بعبده)

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r4.claim: These readers use fatḥa on the mīm of yā ibn umm; the others use kasra.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم: يابن أم بفتح الميم

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r6.claim: Kasra treats ibn and umm as an iḍāfa; the compound vocative is joined like khamsata ʿashara, though this construction implies wāw, while that numeral implies lām. It is common in ibn umm and ibn ʿamm.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r6.anchor: والكسر على الإضافة لأنه بنى (ابن) مع (أم) فجعلا بمنزلة اسم واحد باتصال الثاني بالأول اتصال (خمسة عشر)

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r7.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r7.claim: The cited verse illustrates the frequent vocative compound ibn ʿamm.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: رجال ونسوان يودون أنني ... وإياك نخزى يا ابن عم ونفضح

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r8.claim: The yāʾ can be omitted as in the address yā ghulām, aqbil.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r8.anchor: وحذف الياء كقولك: يا غلام أقبل

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r9.claim: Fatḥa represents an underlying yā ibn ammā, with the alif omitted; the cited poem's yā bint ʿammā means yā bint ʿammī.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r9.anchor: فأما الفتح فعلى تقدير: يابن أما، فحذف الألف، قال الشاعر: يا بنت عما لا تلومي واهجعي

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r10.claim: Raqīb can mean guardian or one who waits; raqibt means I waited, and mirqab is a high place where a watcher stands.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r10.anchor: والرقيب: الحافظ والمنتظر، رقبت أرقب رقبة ورقبانا إذا انتظرت، والمرقب المكان العالي

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r11.claim: One view treats ruqbā and ʿumrā as the same; another calls ruqbā invalid but permits ʿumrā.

JISHUMI:v7p4722/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions say a ruqbā gift, where whichever party dies first determines ownership, is invalid; in an ʿumrā, the gift is valid but a condition returning it to the donor on the donor's earlier death is void.
JISHUMI:v7p4722/r12.anchor: وهذا قول أبي حنيفة وأصحابه، ومنه: أرقبت فلانا داري

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r5.claim: One view is that Moses and Aaron were full brothers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r6.claim: Another view is that they shared a father but not a mother; Aaron said “son of my mother” to soften and appeal to Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r6.anchor: أنه كان أخاه لأبيه دون أمه , وإنما قال يا ابن أم ترفيقا له واستعطافا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses seized Aaron's hair with his right hand and his beard with his left.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r7.anchor: أنه أخذ شعره بيمينه , ولحيته بيسراه , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r8.claim: Another view says Moses took Aaron by the ear and beard, with “head” standing for ear among those who count the ear as part of the head.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r8.anchor: أنه أخذ بأذنه ولحيته , فعبر عن الأذن بالرأس , وهو قول من جعل الأذن من الرأس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r9.claim: One proposed reason for Moses seizing Aaron is that Moses wanted to whisper about the Tablets' descent and conceal them from Israel before repentance; Aaron asked him not to confuse his secret.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r9.anchor: ليسر إليه نزول الألواح عليه , لأنها نزلت عليه في هذه المناجاة . وأراد أن يخفيها عن بني إسرائيل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r10.claim: A second proposed reason is that Moses thought Aaron sided with Israel over the calf, but the author says such a thought is impermissible for prophets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r10.anchor: الثاني : فعل ذلك لأنه وقع في نفسه أن هارون مائل إلى بني إسرئيل فيما فعلوه من أمر العجل , ومثل هذا لا يجوز على الأنبياء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r11.claim: The likeliest reason is that Moses seized Aaron for refraining from condemning the calf worshipers and remaining among their sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r11.anchor: الثالث : وهو الأشبه - أنه فعل ذلك لإمساكه عن الإنكار على بني إسرئيل الذين عبدوا العجل ومقامه بينهم على معاصيهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r12.claim: Aaron's answer may mean that Moses divided Israel through disagreement in their beliefs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r12.anchor: فرقت بينهم بما وقع من اختلاف معتقدهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r13.claim: Alternatively, Moses would have divided them by fighting those who worshiped the calf.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r13.anchor: الثاني : [ فرقت ] بينهم بقتال من عبد العجل

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r14.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r14.claim: Muqatil explains it as “you did not act according to my instruction.”

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r15.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains it as “you did not wait for my instruction.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r15.anchor: لم تنتظر عهدي , قاله أبو عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r16.claim: A report says all Israel worshiped the calf except twelve thousand who remained with Aaron.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p419/r16.anchor: وقيل : إنهم عبدوه جميعا إلا اثني عشر ألفا بقوا مع هارون لم يعبدوه

MUQATIL:20:94-97/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r1.claim: Aaron is the speaker, addressing Moses as his mother’s son.
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r1.anchor: هارون لموسى عليهما السلام: { يبنؤم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي }

MUQATIL:20:94-97/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r2.claim: Aaron explains that if he had objected, the Israelites would have split into factions and killed one another.
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r2.anchor: فإنى لو أنكرت لصاروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا

MUQATIL:20:94-97/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r3.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel and disregarding the instruction to succeed him and set things right (7:142).
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r3.anchor: يقول: ولم تحفظ وصيتى فى الأعراف قوله سبحانه لهارون:

MUQATIL:20:94-97/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r4.claim: Aaron was more beloved to the Israelites than Moses; out of love for Aaron, they named seventy thousand of their children after him.
MUQATIL:20:94-97/r4.anchor: وكان هارون أحب بنى إسرائيل من موسى، صلى الله عليهما، ولقد سمت بنو إسرائيل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r1.claim: Shāmī and Kufan readers other than Ḥafṣ read the mīm with kasra.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r1.anchor: ويخفض الميم شامي وكوفي غير حفص

NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r2.claim: Although most say Aaron shared both parents with Moses, Moses mentions their mother to appeal to tenderness.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r2.anchor: ﴿ قال يا ابن أم ﴾ ويخفض الميم شامي وكوفي غير حفص وكان لأبيه وامه عند الجمهور

NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r3.claim: Moses feared Aaron would accuse him of dividing Israel by fighting some against others, or by leaving one group with Aaron while another followed the Samiri.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر عذره فقال ﴿ إني خشيت أن تقول ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r4.claim: Lam tarqub means “you did not preserve my instruction,” to succeed me among my people and set things right; the passage supports the permissibility of juristic reasoning.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p65#7/r4.anchor: ﴿ ولم ترقب ﴾ ولم تحفظ ﴿ قولي ﴾ اخلفني في قومي واصلح وفيه دليل على جواز الاجتهاد

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses held Aaron's hair in his right hand and beard in his left, overcome by zeal for God; Aaron asks him to stop lest people think it contempt or punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: أخذ شعره بيمينه ولحيته بيساره لأن الغيرة في الله ملكته

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r2.claim: Another view says Moses acted neither contemptuously nor as punishment, but handled Aaron's beard as one might handle one's own; God knows the Prophet's intent.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r2.anchor: وقد قيل: إن موسى عليه السلام إنما فعل هذا على غير استخفاف ولا عقوبة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r3.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel: leaving with Moses would split the people between him and the calf, and could cause bloodshed.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r3.anchor: أي خشيت أن أخرج وأتركهم وقد أمرتني أن أخرج معهم

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r4.claim: Aaron also feared that if he restrained the people and fighting resulted, Moses would blame him; this answers Moses' question about disobeying his command.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r4.anchor: وخشيت إن زجرتهم أن يقع قتال فتلومني على ذلك. وهذا جواب هارون لموسى عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r5.claim: Aaron's explanation is connected to his plea in al-Aʿraf that Israel had overpowered him and nearly killed him, and Moses had ordered him to remain with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r5.anchor: إن القوم استضعفوني وكادوا يقتلونني فلا تشمت بي الأعداء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r6.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r6.claim: Muqatil explains lam tarqub qawli as failing to act on Moses' instruction to preserve the people by staying among them.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r6.anchor: لأنك أمرتني أن أكون معهم قاله مقاتل

QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda explains the phrase as not waiting for Moses' covenant or arrival.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:94-96/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: لم تنتظر عهدي وقدومي

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r1.claim: Umm can mean one's immediate or ancestral mother, or more broadly any origin, source, upbringing, repair, or beginning of something.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r1.anchor: الأم بازاء الأب وهي الوالدة القريبة التي ولدته والبعيدة التي ولدت من ولدته

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r2.claim: The original form is yā ibn ummī; the yāʾ changes to alif and is then dropped, retaining the fatḥa because the expression is frequent and lengthy and the doubled consonant is heavy.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r2.anchor: وأصله يا ابن أمي أبدل الياء ألفا فقيل : يا ابن أما ثم حذف الألف

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r3.claim: A reading has yā ibn umm with the final yāʾ omitted and its kasra retained.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r3.anchor: وقرىء يا ابن أم بالكسر بحذف الياء والاكتفاء بالكسرة

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r4.claim: Calling him son of my mother honors the mother, softens Aaron's heart, invokes their kinship, and signals that they shared a womb.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r4.anchor: وخص الأم بالإضافة استعظاما لحقها وترقيقا لقلبه واعتدادا لنسبها

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r5.claim: The majority hold that Moses and Aaron had both the same father and mother.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r5.anchor: وإلا فالجمهور عل أنهما لأب وأم

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r6.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r6.claim: Some Sufi masters say Aaron's prophethood came from the presence of mercy, and Moses calls him son of his mother because mercy and nurturing are associated with mothers.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r6.anchor: قال بعض الكبار كانت نبوة هارون من حضرة الرحمة

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r7.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya portrays Moses returning from the divine presence overwhelmed by longing and intimacy, while Aaron humbles himself to soften him through their maternal bond and recall the Sinai encounter when Moses fainted after asking to see God.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : لما رأى هارون موسى رجع من تلك الحضرة

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r8.claim: The same esoteric account says Aaron's appeal recalls Moses fainting at the mountain and angels dragging his head while reproaching the mismatch between dust and the Lord of Lords.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r8.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : لما رأى هارون موسى رجع من تلك الحضرة

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r9.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r9.claim: Hafez's Persian verses picture the Simurgh's lofty nest as beyond ordinary hunters and their weak traps, extending the image of an inaccessible exalted station.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r9.anchor: قال الحافظ : برو اين دام برمرغ دكرنه كه عنقارا بلنداست آشيانه

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r10.claim: A report says Moses seized Aaron's head hair with his right hand and beard with his left in intense anger; seeing the calf worship, he could not restrain himself and acted before the people.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r10.anchor: روي أنه أخذ شعر رأسه بيمينه ولحيته بشماله من شدة غيظه

BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r11.claim: Aaron feared that if he fought some Israelites against others, Moses would accuse him of dividing the people; fighting could cause a separation from which they would never reunite.
BURSEVI:v5p321#2/r11.anchor: إنى خشيت} لو قاتلت بعضهم ببعض وتفرقوا {أن تقول فرقت

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r1.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r1.claim: Al-Jalalayn says Aaron feared that leaving the Israelites to follow Moses would split them into fighting factions, after which Moses would blame him.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r1.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : خشيت إن فارقتهم واتبعتك أن يصيروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا فتقول : أوقعت الفرق فيما بينهم

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r2.claim: Aaron had not preserved Moses’ charge to succeed him well: unite the people, preserve cohesion, and deal gently until Moses returned, especially given their strength and the leaders’ weakness.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r2.anchor: يريد به قوله : {اخلفنى فى قومى وأصلح} فإن الإصلاح ضم النشر وحفظ جماعات الناس والمداراة بهم

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r3.speaker: العيون
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r3.claim: Al-ʿUyūn glosses the phrase as not considering Moses’ situation or not waiting for his return.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r3.anchor: وفي "العيون" : أي : لم تنظر في أمري أو لم تنتظر قدومي

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r4.claim: Al-Tawīlāt al-Najmiyya says waiting for Moses’ word and obeying him kept Aaron from following him; this was not disobedience.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r4.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يعني منعني ترقب قولك وإطاعة أمرك عن اتباعك لا عصيان أمرك

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r5.claim: Aaron is excusing himself: excuses include denying the deed, explaining it to remove guilt, or admitting it and resolving not to repeat it; the last is repentance, so every repentance is an excuse but not vice versa.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r5.anchor: وهذا الكلام من هارون اعتذار والعذر تحرى الإنسان ما يمحو به ذنوبه وذلك ثلاثة أضرب

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r6.claim: Aaron was forbearing and gentle, which explains why the Israelites especially loved him.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r6.anchor: حليما رفيقا ولذا كان بنو إسرائيل أشد حباله

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r7.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r7.claim: ʿAlī calls love in people’s hearts the finest of treasures.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r7.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه أحسن الكنوز محبة القلوب

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r8.speaker: سقراط
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r8.claim: Socrates says good character brings a pleasant life, safety, and love, while poor character sours life and earns hatred.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r8.anchor: قال سقراط : من أحسن خلقه طابت عيشته ودامت سلامته وتأكدت في النفوس محبته

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r9.speaker: بزرجمهر
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r9.claim: Buzurjmihr links contentment with comfort and humility with love, adding that forbearance may appear weak in some settings but brings glory in others.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r9.anchor: قال بزرجمهر ثمرة القناعة الراحة وثمرة التواضع المحبة

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r10.speaker: أرسطو
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r10.claim: Aristotle says eloquence raises rank, humility wins love, forbearance gains supporters, gentleness wins hearts, and fidelity sustains brotherhood.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r10.anchor: قال أرسطو بإصابة المنطق يعظم القدر وبالتواضع تكثر المحبة وبالحلم تكثر الأنصار

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r11.claim: The Prophet remained gentle and kind, matching his description as compassionate and merciful toward believers.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r11.anchor: وكان النبي عليه السلام لم يخرج عن حد اللين والرفق

BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r12.claim: The author cites the Mathnawī portraying God’s servants as merciful and patient, bearing divine qualities while gently helping in reform.
BURSEVI:v5p321#3/r12.anchor: بندكان حق رحيم وبردبار خوى حق دارند در اصلاح كارمهربان بى رشوتان يارى كران

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

NASHR:v2p163/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p163/r2.speaker: آخرون
NASHR:v2p163/r2.claim: Some authorities reach 216 by additionally counting ألا تتبعن in Ṭā Hā and إن يردن الرحمن in Yā Sīn.
NASHR:v2p163/r2.anchor: وهما ألا تتبعن في طه إن يردن الرحمن في يس فجعلوها مائتين وست عشرة

DURR-FULL:v5p587/r7.claim: Aaron remained with the believers, listening and obeying, because he feared Moses would accuse him of splitting Israel and disregarding his instruction.
DURR-FULL:v5p587/r7.anchor: فأقام هرون فيمن معه من المسلمين مخافة أن يقول له موسى: {فرقت بين بني إسرائيل ولم ترقب قولي} وكان له سامعا مطيعا
